nodes.summary: There exist a finite group $G$ and a Hall subgroup $H$ of $G$ (that is, the order $|H|$ is coprime to the index $|G : H|$) such that $H$ is not pronormal in its normal closure $\langle H^G \rangle$, the smallest normal subgroup of $G$ containing $H$: for some $g \in \langle H^G \rangle$, no element $x$ of the subgroup $\langle H, gHg^{-1} \rangle$ generated by $H$ and $gHg^{-1}$ satisfies $xHx^{-1} = gHg^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Hall subgroups need not be pronormal in their normal closure

nodes.summary: This is the statement that for every finite group $G$ and every Hall subgroup $H$ of $G$ (a subgroup whose order $|H|$ is coprime to its index $|G : H|$), $H$ is pronormal in its normal closure $\langle H^G \rangle$, the smallest normal subgroup of $G$ containing $H$: for every $g \in \langle H^G \rangle$ there is an element $x$ of the subgroup $\langle H, gHg^{-1} \rangle$ generated by $H$ and $gHg^{-1}$ with…
nodes.title: Vdovin–Revin question on Hall subgroups and their normal closures

nodes.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a Hall subgroup when its order $|H|$ is coprime to its index $|G : H|$.
nodes.title: Hall subgroups (order coprime to index)

nodes.summary: Let $H$ and $K$ be subgroups of a group $G$. Then $H$ is pronormal in $K$ when for every $g \in K$ there is an element $x$ of the subgroup $\langle H, gHg^{-1} \rangle$ generated by $H$ and $gHg^{-1}$ such that $xHx^{-1} = gHg^{-1}$, that is, $H$ and its conjugate $gHg^{-1}$ are conjugate by an element of $\langle H, gHg^{-1} \rangle$.
nodes.title: Pronormality in a subgroup
